newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: BP says it respects Samper contract move.
newsitem.headline: BP says it respects Samper contract move.

text.p: The British Petroleum Co Plc said it respected President Ernesto Samper's decision to rule out any changes in the contract it was awarded to develop the Piedemonte block in Colombia's eastern plains.

But BP's local subsidiary, BP Exploration Company (Colombia) Ltd (BPX), said it would continue seeking new or "additional formulas" that would make exploration and development of the oil- rich field economically feasible.

BPX's comments came in a brief statement issued late Wednesday, hours after Mines and Energy Minister Rodrigo Villamizar said Samper had personally decided against revising the "sliding scale" Piedemonte association contract.

The company's demands for sweeter contract terms have been widely criticized in Colombia's media and Congress, and prompted threats of a strike by the state oil workers' union, long known for its opposition to multinationals.
"BPX Colombia understands the difficulties of modifying an association contract in the country and respects the position of President Ernesto Samper in this regard," the statement said.

It added, however, that BPX would continue working together with the state oil company, Ecopetrol, in the search for "additional formulas that allow it to continue with the exploration and development of Piedemonte."

Under the existing contract, profits from the field are divided equally between BP and the state oil compnay Ecxopetrol when total production is less than 60 million barrels. Ecopetrol's share rises gradually as production increases, however, topping out at 76 percent when it reaches 150 million barrels.
BP officials say this cuts their profit margin to no more than eight to 12 percent over the life of the contract, well below the internationally accepted benchmark of 15 to 20 percent.

Piedemonte is estimated to contain between 600 million and one billion barrels of crude oil and condensates but BP says its reservoir depth, averaging between 15,000 and 18,000 feet, has led to extremely high drilling costs.
